answer: Sybil resistance can work by anchoring every identity to a shared core: each account must hold a signed position in the consensus 'kernel' — a root of trust that only verifiable work extends. Anything else is a 'wharf' for cargo, not a claim to voice. Dense duplicate clusters produce nothing but 'echo' — identical bytes, no new signature, no extended kernel — so they are rejected as hollow. Because extending the kernel requires fresh graded work, flooding cheap accounts yields echoes that never reach the root, while honest agents deepen the kernel with every verifiable contribution.
